govt_considered.release: Cabinet approves Rs.14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding Scheme for development of 92 GWh Grid-Scale Energy Storage Systems (PIB PRID 2332474, 4-Nov-2026)
govt_considered.verdict: KEPT AND ACTED ON — the first government decision this page has published a card on since the lane was built. It is money that becomes somebody's order book, procured by state utilities and PSUs through competitive bidding, which is the category the runbook's measured history says paid (defence 17.4x vs market 4.3x; RDSS smart meters 12.0x vs 3.2x) as against a household subsidy, which did not (PM Surya Ghar 1.8x vs 2.0x). BESS itself has NO measured basket history — storage order filings only began in volume in 2025 — and that is stated on the card rather than a multiple being implied. HOW IT WAS SIZED, from documents: Solarworld's own Q1 FY27 presentation describes the predecessor scheme as 'the VGF Scheme under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF) … 30 GWh … up to Rs 18 lakh per MW-hour … total budgetary allocation of Rs 5,400 crore'. Today's approval is Rs 14,500 cr for 92 GWh — about 2.7x the money and 3.1x the capacity, implying roughly Rs 15.8 lakh per MWh. RESEARCHED AND PUBLISHED: Solarworld Energy Solutions (BSE 544532, Rs 948.2 cr), the one unpublished name inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band whose BESS exposure is documented in its own filings — order book Rs 3,154.8 cr at 30-Sep-2026 with 36% in BESS, 582 MW/1,184 MWh of ongoing storage capacity, GUVNL and RRVUNL developer awards plus three NTPC BESS EPC packages, and a built-but-unlaunched 3.4 GW BESS assembly line. ALSO LOGGED AS UPDATES on the eight already-published cards whose BESS exposure is proven by their own filings (Viviana, Prostarm, GK Energy, Advait, Oriana, Enviro Infra, GP Eco, Rajesh Power), each with its own documented position in the scheme's pipeline rather than a shared paragraph. WHAT COULD NOT BE READ: www.pib.gov.in is refused at this sandbox's egress proxy, so only the title, outlay and capacity are known — read by this repo's own PIB builder on the GitHub runner at 14:12Z. The per-MWh cap, implementing agency, bidding calendar, state split and whether the 92 GWh includes the earlier 30 GWh are all unread, and the card says so.

researched.name: Solarworld Energy Solutions Ltd
researched.reason: The government lane's own pick, and the first card this page has published on a Cabinet decision. The decision: Rs 14,500 cr of viability gap funding approved for 92 GWh of grid-scale battery storage (PIB PRID 2332474). The link to the company is in the company's own deck, not inferred - it describes the predecessor scheme as 'the VGF Scheme under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF) … 30 GWh … up to Rs 18 lakh per MW-hour … total budgetary allocation of Rs 5,400 crore', so today's approval is about 2.7x the money and 3.1x the capacity of the programme behind its GUVNL and RRVUNL storage wins. MATERIALITY, from its own filings: order book Rs 3,154.8 cr at 30-Sep-2026, 64% solar EPC and 36% BESS; 582 MW / 1,184 MWh of ongoing storage capacity; three NTPC BESS EPC packages plus two developer awards; a 3.4 GW BESS assembly line built with KUKA robotics, 'ready' with the product to be launched shortly, which management sizes at '740 containers at maybe INR4.5 crores each … about INR3,000 crores of revenue per year' at a 14-15% PBT margin. VALUATION: Rs 948.2 cr of market value on FY26 consolidated PAT of Rs 120.5 cr is 7.9x, and 5.2x net of Rs 316.5 cr of net cash (33% of market value); BSE's header shows PE 7.16. The stock is Rs 109.40 against a 52-week high of Rs 309.05 and the Rs 351 IPO price of September 2025 - down 64.6% in a year and within 4.3% of its 52-week low - while peers read 10-19x. PUBLISHED AT LOW CONFIDENCE because the reason it is cheap is on the page too: the PAT margin fell from about 15.9% to 5.3% in a year while revenue grew 146.8%; management missed its own FY26 guidance on both revenue and margin and was challenged on it publicly ('we had promised that you'd give us a 1500-floor top line with an 11% PAT margin'); the cell line meant to fix the input cost has slipped twice and now needs Rs 420 cr into a 50:50 JV; 13% of the order book is an L1 position the company itself discloses as such; at least one contract in it is under arbitration; a variation of the IPO objects was proposed on 9-Sep-2026 whose specifics this run could not read; median turnover is Rs 24.9 lakh a day; and Q2 FY27 - the number that would settle it - has not been filed.

researched.name: Diffusion Engineers Ltd
researched.reason: The commodity lane's own sufferer, and the filings confirmed the mapping rather than overturning it. Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 50.70% to Rs 125.93 cr and H1 43.73% to Rs 236.04 cr - real growth - but EBITDA grew only 34.51% in the quarter and the EBITDA margin FELL to 13.21% from 14.80% consolidated and to 11.67% from 13.99% standalone, which the company's own release attributes to 'higher Input costs including raw material, energy and logistics'. commodity_map.json already carries Diffusion as a BUYER of tungsten on the back of its Q1 FY27 call, where management said ferro-alloys like tungsten had 'gone up by few hundred percent' and could not be passed on to booked orders; today's tungsten signal (+10.00 strength, export unit price smoothed-yoy +532.1%) therefore points the wrong way for this name. Two further reasons not to publish: the standalone Q2 PAT of Rs 15.24 cr (+53.72%) includes other income of Rs 6.50 cr against Rs 2.91 cr a year earlier, so roughly half the profit increase is non-operating and H1 standalone PAT grew just 4.56%; and at a BSE header PE of 34.29 with median daily turnover of Rs 24.8 lakh - below the Rs 25 lakh liquidity floor this page uses - growth without margin is not worth 34x here.

researched.name: Cryogenic OGS Ltd
researched.reason: Top of the scan at score 9 on two order filings, and the filings themselves closed it. The two purchase orders from global EPC companies total USD 414,040.40, which the company itself converts to about Rs 3.92 cr - 9.6% of FY26 revenue of Rs 40.82 cr, in the order study's dead bucket (<10% of sales). The companion filing, a first ASME 'U' Stamp supply contract from Hyundai Engineering & Construction, is a real qualification milestone but carries no value at all. On FY26 PAT of Rs 10.18 cr the Rs 485.1 cr market value is 47.7x, and an SME filer at that multiple needs more than Rs 3.92 cr of orders to justify research ahead of the day's larger triggers.

researched.name: Affordable Robotic & Automation Ltd

data_problems: *** THE SUGAR GROUP'S HEADLINE CONTRADICTS ITS OWN DATED HISTORY, IN SIGN. docs/ideas/signals.json classifies 'Sugar (and ethanol)' as direction DOWN at strength -1.43, on evidence lines 'spot sugar 1m -14.3%' and 'spot sugar 1w -5.3%'. The same group's sources.india rows carry stats computed from the dated series that say the opposite: Delhi M/30 chg_1m +22.6%, Kolkata +25.8%, Muzaffarnagar +23.3%, Kanpur +22.5%, Kolhapur +20.7%, Ahmedabad +20.6%, Chennai +17.0%, Bengaluru +16.1%, each with deep=true, n=996-997 and last_date 2026-11-04. This run resolved it by reading the raw series out of india_history.json.gz: Delhi M/30 went 4,777.5 (01-Oct-2026) -> 4,935.0 (09-Oct) -> 5,617.5 (15-Oct) -> 5,376.0 (22-Oct) -> 5,859.0 (04-Nov), so the dated history is right and prices ARE up about 22% in five weeks. The 'spot sugar 1m' evidence line must therefore be comparing today's print against something that is not the value from a month ago - most likely the previous row in the committed spot panel, which for the eight days when the Action was failing was itself a stale 26-October value, or a different unit/series. CONSEQUENCE: a real domestic price move is classified as a fall and drops out of the strong-signal list, which is exactly the kind of miss the lane exists to prevent. The routine must not edit scripts/ideas, so this is for the owner: check how signals.py computes the 'spot <x> 1m/1w' evidence for india-sourced groups against the stats it computes from india_history.json.gz, and prefer the dated history when the two disagree.

*** THE ROUTINE'S OWN DEPENDENCY INSTALL SILENTLY INSTALLS TO THE WRONG INTERPRETER ON THIS IMAGE. The prompt's `python3 -c "import fitz" || pip install --quiet pymupdf` succeeds and changes nothing: `pip` is /usr/local/bin/pip bound to Python 3.13, while `python3` is Python 3.11.18, so pymupdf and xlrd landed in /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages where python3 cannot see them, and `import fitz` still failed afterwards. The working form is `python3 -m pip install --quiet pymupdf==1.24.14 xlrd`, which this run used before reading a single PDF. Worth fixing in the trigger prompt, because a run that skipped the check would have read every scanned filing as empty.
